svg.title: Four simpler compute paths: Elastic Beanstalk, Lightsail, Batch and Outposts
svg.desc: Four cards in two rows. AWS Elastic Beanstalk: you bring your web application's code; AWS sets up EC2 instances or an EKS cluster, load balancing, scaling and health monitoring, in your account; you pay nothing extra, only for the resources it creates; pick it when you want to deploy code without building the setup by hand. Amazon Lightsail: you bring a website or small app, often from a ready-made image such as WordPress; AWS sets up a virtual server with storage, a static IP and data transfer as one bundle; you pay a fixed monthly plan price, charged by the hour up to that maximum; pick it when you want something simple with a predictable bill. AWS Batch: you bring many jobs, each packaged as a container; AWS sets up a queue and compute that grows for the jobs and is removed when they finish; you pay nothing extra, only for the EC2 or Fargate capacity the jobs use; pick it when you have lots of jobs to run, often too long for Lambda. AWS Outposts: you bring a site with space, power and a network connection to an AWS Region; AWS sets up racks or servers of AWS hardware that it monitors, patches and maintains; you pay for a term of years, by configuration; pick it when work or data must stay in your own building. A note says Beanstalk, Batch and Lightsail run on AWS servers that still exist; you just don't assemble them yourself.
